summary: A Zoom OAuth app is easy to build and test in your own account, but any public or unlisted app must pass a dedicated, multi-part Marketplace review before it can be distributed. That review covers submission completeness, branding, functionality and usability, compliance, and a security review that tests against the OWASP Top 10 and checks for least-privilege scopes. Plan for a review cycle measured in weeks.

oauthAvailability.note: OAuth 2.0 apps are built in the Zoom App Marketplace. Public and unlisted apps require review before distribution.
alternatives: Account-level (admin-managed) apps that remain private to one account

difficulty.reason: Public/unlisted apps must pass a multi-part Marketplace review including a security review against the OWASP Top 10.

approvalWait.note: Review time varies with app quality, scope clarity, and listing completeness.

timeEstimate.criticalPath: The multi-part Marketplace review (functionality, compliance, and security testing) dominates the timeline.

review.requiredWhen: Required for public and unlisted apps before they can be distributed. A private app used only in your own account can skip the Marketplace review.

stages.name: Submission completeness & branding
stages.description: Zoom checks metadata, technical design docs, security information, and branding guideline compliance.

stages.name: Functionality, usability & compliance
stages.description: Reviewers verify install/uninstall, configuration, data flow, UX, and compliance with privacy requirements.

stages.name: Security review
stages.description: Technical design review, OAuth scope evaluation for least privilege, and security testing against the OWASP Top 10.

prerequisites.item: A Zoom account and Marketplace developer access
prerequisites.detail: Apps are built and submitted in the Zoom App Marketplace.
Required for submission completeness and the security review.

prerequisites.item: A clear test plan and test credentials
prerequisites.detail: Well-defined scopes and clear listing content shorten review time.

steps.title: Create an OAuth app in the Marketplace
steps.detail: In the Zoom App Marketplace, create an OAuth app (user-level or account-level) and configure your redirect URL and app credentials.

steps.title: Select least-privilege scopes
steps.detail: Add only the scopes your features require. The security review verifies the app requests the minimum necessary scopes and may ask you to remove unused ones.
steps.gotcha: Poorly described or over-broad scopes lengthen the review; define each scope's purpose clearly.

steps.title: Implement and test the OAuth flow
steps.detail: Implement the authorization code flow, verify install/uninstall and configuration, and test end-to-end data flow as a reviewer would.

steps.title: Complete the build flow and submit for review
steps.detail: Fill in metadata, technical design, and security information, then submit. Expect a remediation report if the app does not pass, which you address and resubmit.

notes: The OAuth redirect URL is configured on the app in the Marketplace.
Use an HTTPS redirect that matches your deployed callback exactly.

sensitive.consequence: Access to cloud recordings; reviewers scrutinize data handling of recordings.
Admin-level user management; requires account admin and heightened review.

notes: The security review verifies least-privilege scope usage and may require removing unused scopes.
Granular (per-resource) scopes are preferred over broad classic scopes.

blockers.title: App rejected in review
blockers.symptom: Zoom returns a remediation report instead of approving the app.
blockers.cause: Functionality, usability, compliance, or security testing found issues.
blockers.resolution: Complete every action item in the remediation report and resubmit.

blockers.title: Scopes flagged as over-broad
blockers.symptom: Reviewers ask you to remove or justify scopes.
blockers.cause: The app requested more scopes than its functionality justifies.
blockers.resolution: Remove unused scopes and clearly describe the purpose of each remaining scope.

blockers.title: Security testing failures
blockers.symptom: The app fails OWASP Top 10 or vulnerable-library checks.
blockers.cause: Security testing surfaced vulnerabilities or outdated dependencies.
blockers.resolution: Remediate findings, update vulnerable libraries, and resubmit for security review.

agentCan: Implement the OAuth authorization code flow and token refresh
Wire the least-privilege scope set and redirect route
Draft the technical design and scope-justification documentation
humanMust: Own the Marketplace app and submission
Provide security information and respond to the remediation report
handoffPoints: Agent builds and documents the app; a human submits and drives the multi-part review.

difficulty.note: Public/unlisted apps undergo a dedicated multi-part review.

timeEstimate.note: Review time varies and is not a fixed SLA per the review-process page.

review.note: Review stages (completeness, functionality, security) from the review-process page.

prerequisites.note: Submission completeness requires technical design and security info.

steps.note: OAuth setup from the OAuth guide; submission from the review-process page.

redirectUris.note: Redirect URL configuration from the OAuth guide.

scopes.note: Least-privilege scope evaluation documented in the security review.

blockers.note: Remediation and OWASP testing documented in the review-process page.

agentHandoff.note: Author judgment on the agent/human split.
